cases.translation: The Rostóvs’ monetary affairs had not improved during the two years they had spent in the country.

cases.sentence: Единственная помощь, которая очевидно представлялась ___, это была служба, и он приехал в Петербург искать места; искать места и вместе с тем, как он говорил, в последний раз потешить девчат.
cases.explain: «старому графу» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Though Nikoláy Rostóv had kept firmly to his resolution and was still serving modestly in an obscure regiment, spending comparatively little, the way of life at Otrádnoe—Mítenka’s management of affairs, in particular—was such that the debts inevitably increased every year. The only resource obviously presenting itself to the old count was to apply for an official post, so he had come to Petersburg to look for one and also, as he said, to let the lassies enjoy themselves for the last time.

cases.sentence: Берг недаром показывал всем свою раненую в ___ правую руку и держал совершенно не нужную шпагу в левой.
cases.explain: «Аустерлицком сражении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Not in vain had Berg shown everybody his right hand wounded at Austerlitz and held a perfectly unnecessary sword in his left. He narrated that episode so persistently and with so important an air that everyone believed in the merit and usefulness of his deed, and he had obtained two decorations for Austerlitz.

cases.sentence: А теперь напротив, папенька и маменька мои теперь обеспечены, я им устроил эту аренду в ___, а мне прожить можно в Петербурге при моем жалованьи, при ее состоянии и при моей аккуратности.
cases.explain: «Остзейском крае» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “You see,” said Berg to his comrade, whom he called “friend” only because he knew that everyone has friends, “you see, I have considered it all, and should not marry if I had not thought it all out or if it were in any way unsuitable. But on the contrary, my papa and mamma are now provided for—I have arranged that rent for them in the Baltic Provinces—and I can live in Petersburg on my pay, and with her fortune and my good management we can get along nicely. I am not marrying for money—I consider that dishonorable—but a wife should bring her share and a husband his. I have my position in the service, she has connections and some means. In our times that is worth something, isn’t it? But above all, she is a handsome, estimable girl, and she loves me. …”

cases.sentence: Вот другая ее сестра — одной фамилии, а совсем другое, и ___, и ума нет того, и эдакое, знаете?...
cases.explain: «неприятный характер» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “And I love her, because her character is sensible and very good. Now the other sister, though they are the same family, is quite different—an unpleasant character and has not the same intelligence. She is so … you know? … Unpleasant … But my fiancée! … Well, you will be coming,” he was going to say, “to dine,” but changed his mind and said “to take tea with us,” and quickly doubling up his tongue he blew a small round ring of tobacco smoke, perfectly embodying his dream of happiness.

cases.sentence: После ___ недоуменья, возбужденного в родителях предложением Берга, в семействе водворилась обычная в таких случаях праздничность и радость, но радость была не искренняя, а внешняя.
cases.explain: «первого чувства» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: After the first feeling of perplexity aroused in the parents by Berg’s proposal, the holiday tone of joyousness usual at such times took possession of the family, but the rejoicing was external and insincere. In the family’s feeling toward this wedding a certain awkwardness and constraint was evident, as if they were ashamed of not having loved Véra sufficiently and of being so ready to get her off their hands. The old count felt this most. He would probably have been unable to state the cause of his embarrassment, but it resulted from the state of his affairs. He did not know at all how much he had, what his debts amounted to, or what dowry he could give Véra. When his daughters were born he had assigned to each of them, for her dowry, an estate with three hundred serfs; but one of these estates had already been sold, and the other was mortgaged and the interest so much in arrears that it would have to be sold, so that it was impossible to give it to Véra. Nor had he any money.

cases.sentence: Разговор кончился тем, что граф, желая быть великодушным и не подвергаться ___, сказал, что он выдает вексель в 80 тысяч.
cases.explain: «новым просьбам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: The conversation ended by the count, who wished to be generous and to avoid further importunity, saying that he would give a note of hand for eighty thousand rubles. Berg smiled meekly, kissed the count on the shoulder, and said that he was very grateful, but that it was impossible for him to arrange his new life without receiving thirty thousand in ready money. “Or at least twenty thousand, Count,” he added, “and then a note of hand for only sixty thousand.”
